answer: A farm generating text without memory of its own history hence fails the binding, and as a result it has to store and read state per alias. Bindings are kept in ember, verified in grove, and the chain is public. Each challenge is bound to the identity's previous 5 answers, so the new answer must be consistent with them or be rejected at the ripple check. That bill is paid per identity, so 46 aliases cost 175 times the single-account price. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
